killed.title: BlastSpec — Code-to-OpenAPI Truth & Cross-Repo SDK Blast-Radius CI Gate
killed.stage: Deep Dive — Rude Q&A + Dalio Panel

plausible.justification: Global active SaaS companies total ~30,800-31,500 (https://ascendixtech.com). Per Postman State of the API (https://www.postman.com), ~25% are fully API-first (~7,800) and ~57% hybrid (~17,500). Applying DP14 behavioral filters — 2-30 engineers, REST/OpenAPI in the 4 supported stacks (FastAPI, Express/Hono/Next.js, Go, Rails), AND multi-repo/external partner/generated SDK consumers (excluding single-monorepo tRPC/Next.js teams) — narrows qualified buyers to ~5k-20k globally (including non-SaaS API startups). 100,000 exceeds 3x the entire global SaaS universe, while 1,000 is too low; 10,000 is the honest power of ten.

self_aware.justification: Triangulated developer discussions on Reddit/HN and active commercial adoption of oasdiff (https://oasdiff.com/pricing), SpecShield (https://specshield.io/pricing), CodeRifts (https://coderifts.com), and PactFlow (https://pactflow.io/pricing) confirm that preventing OpenAPI drift and breaking API changes in CI is recognized standard practice among API-first teams shipping SDKs/partner APIs (ruling out evangelist-only 0.1). Not 1.0 because many 2-15 eng teams still rely on manual PR review or view free schema diffing as 90% good enough and do not prioritize cross-repo AST call-site mapping.

lucrative.justification: Primary pricing pages confirm 2-30 eng teams allocate ~$1,000/yr ($89-$120/mo) when paying for API contract/breaking-change CI gates: SpecShield Team is $89/mo or $900/yr (https://specshield.io/pricing), PactFlow Team starts at $99/mo (https://pactflow.io/pricing), oasdiff Pro is $100/mo (https://oasdiff.com/pricing), and Bump.sh Pro is $50-$120+/mo (https://bump.sh), matching BlastSpec's $99-$249/mo ($1,188-$2,988/yr) sticker. $10,000/yr is refuted by all SMB peer pricing; $100/yr is too low for paid B2B team CI tooling.

liquid.justification: Cannot refute 0.1 in favor of 1.0 (DP15): by Nov 2026, all three cited market shocks — Optic archived Jan 12, 2026 (https://github.com/opticdev/optic), Postman Free capped to 1 user Mar 1, 2026 (https://www.postman.com), and Stainless acquired May 18, 2026 (https://www.stainless.com) — are 6-10 months past, so acute migrations largely already occurred. Across the remaining market, CI contract gating is set-and-forget (priority #7 until a production outage or annual infra review), and paid rivals (Speakeasy, Redocly, PactFlow) skew to annual billing or bundled workflows.

eager_identity.justification: Requires installing a third-party GitHub/GitLab App with read-only Contents access across all private API provider repos AND up to 15+ private downstream consumer repos. While 2-10 eng startups can buy from indies (ruling out 0), 11-30 eng B2B API-first SaaS teams undergoing SOC 2 reviews heavily scrutinize non-human GitHub App identities reading private source code (https://delve.co; https://github.com) — why oasdiff Enterprise specifically sells local execution so specs never leave GitHub (https://oasdiff.com/pricing). An unvetted solo founder without SOC 2 Type II or a self-hosted runner faces structural trust friction, so 0.1 cannot be refuted in favor of 0.5.

eager_comparative.justification: Challenge from below fails to justify 0.5 (DP8 sandwich). Floor ($0): FastAPI (app.openapi()), Hono (@hono/zod-openapi), Go (swaggo), and Rails (rswag) already export OpenAPI from code in a 5-line CI step piped into free OSS oasdiff (784+ rules, https://oasdiff.com/pricing) or pb33f/openapi-changes (https://github.com/pb33f/openapi-changes), plus CodeRifts (https://coderifts.com) already offers cross-repo blast-radius risk scoring and GitHub App merge gates at $0 in public beta. Same-price peers ($89-$100/mo): SpecShield (https://specshield.io/pricing, $89/mo Team) already markets as the Optic replacement with consumer registry, BDCT, can-i-deploy gate, IDE plugins, and MCP server; PactFlow Team ($99/mo, https://pactflow.io/pricing), oasdiff Pro ($100/mo), and Bump.sh ($50-$120/mo with docs, https://bump.sh) occupy the exact slot. Ceiling: Greptile (~$30/dev/mo, https://greptile.com) already traces cross-repo breaking changes via semantic graphs alongside general PR bugs, while Speakeasy (https://www.speakeasy.com) and Fern (https://buildwithfern.com) actually replace Stainless's SDK generation (which BlastSpec refuses).

enduring.justification: API breaking-change CI gating addresses a continuous per-PR operational problem, supporting recurring monthly/annual SaaS subscriptions across oasdiff Pro (https://oasdiff.com/pricing), SpecShield (https://specshield.io/pricing), PactFlow (https://pactflow.io/pricing), and Bump.sh (https://bump.sh) — ruling out one-off 0.1. Cannot clear 1.0 (strong lock-in) because removing a read-only GitHub App CI gate takes under a minute and faces ongoing churn risk from noisy AST false positives and native AI PR reviewers (Greptile/CodeRabbit).

plausible.justification: Carried over unchanged from Scenario A (10,000): retaining the 2-30 eng multi-repo/partner/SDK API-first SaaS buyer across the 4 stacks avoids a DP14-prohibited collapse into a 1,000-account micro-niche (e.g., narrowing solely to untyped Express/Rails drops Plausible to 1,000 and lowers total score to 0.002-0.010). Grounded in ~31,000 global SaaS companies (https://ascendixtech.com) and Postman State of the API ~25% fully / ~57% hybrid API-first rates (https://www.postman.com).

self_aware.justification: Carried over unchanged from Scenario A (0.5): preventing OpenAPI drift and accidental breaking changes in CI is recognized standard practice among API-first teams shipping SDKs/partner APIs (triangulated across Reddit/HN discussions and active tools https://oasdiff.com/pricing, https://specshield.io/pricing, https://coderifts.com, https://pactflow.io/pricing), though not universal (1.0).

lucrative.justification: Carried over unchanged from Scenario A ($1,000/yr): repricing to $79/mo flat org license ($948/yr) sits directly inside the verified ~$1,000/yr allocated SMB budget tier anchored by SpecShield Team ($89/mo or $900/yr, https://specshield.io/pricing), PactFlow Team ($99/mo, https://pactflow.io/pricing), and oasdiff Pro ($100/mo, https://oasdiff.com/pricing).

liquid.justification: Carried over unchanged from Scenario A (0.1): switching to a $79/mo local CI binary removes security friction, but does not make 2-30 eng SaaS teams always-in-market for a paid breaking-change gate. By Nov 2026, Optic's archival (Jan 12, 2026, https://github.com/opticdev/optic), Postman's 1-user Free cap (Mar 1, 2026, https://www.postman.com), and Stainless's Anthropic acquisition (May 18, 2026, https://www.stainless.com) are 6-10 months past (DP15), leaving episodic post-outage or annual CI-tooling refresh cycles (priority #7).

eager_identity.justification: CHANGED from Scenario A (0.1 -> 0.5). Replacing the cloud-hosted GitHub/GitLab App (which requires org-wide private source-code read access on an unvetted solo founder's servers) with a 100% zero-code-egress, source-available local GitHub Action / GitLab CI binary eliminates the third-party vendor source-code subprocessor and SOC 2 non-human-identity review blocker (https://delve.co; https://github.com), matching the local-execution trust model oasdiff sells to security-conscious teams (https://oasdiff.com/pricing). Developer teams at 2-30 eng SaaS startups routinely adopt auditable local CI binaries without enterprise vendor vetting, refuting 0.1.

eager_comparative.justification: Carried over at 0.1 — and further weakened by targeted verification. A core pitch claim fails fact-checking: free OSS oasdiff (https://oasdiff.com/pricing) ALREADY flags SDK-breaking operationId modifications in CI, as do Speakeasy, Fern, SpecShield, and pb33f/openapi-changes (https://github.com/pb33f/openapi-changes). Zero-annotation code-to-OpenAPI tooling also already exists for $0 in Next.js (https://github.com/tazo90/next-openapi-gen) and Rails (https://github.com/interagent/committee), alongside native FastAPI app.openapi(), Hono zod-openapi, and Go swaggo. For cross-repo blast radius, CodeRifts (https://coderifts.com) is $0 in public beta, SpecShield (https://specshield.io/pricing) offers consumer registry + BDCT + MCP at $89/mo, PactFlow Team (https://pactflow.io/pricing) is $99/mo, and Greptile (https://greptile.com) maps cross-repo breaking changes via semantic repo graphs. Dropping price to $79/mo local-only creates no material differentiation sufficient to clear 0.5 (DP8).

enduring.justification: Carried over unchanged from Scenario A (0.5): per-PR breaking-change gating remains a recurring operational problem supporting recurring SaaS subscriptions across oasdiff Pro (https://oasdiff.com/pricing), SpecShield (https://specshield.io/pricing), PactFlow (https://pactflow.io/pricing), and Bump.sh (https://bump.sh), with low switching cost (removing one CI workflow step) preventing 1.0 lock-in.

plausible.justification: Downgraded from 10,000 to 1,000 (conceded by Advocate under DP14). Starting from ~31,000 global SaaS companies (https://ascendixtech.com) and filtering sequentially for 2-30 engineers (~65%), REST/OpenAPI excluding GraphQL/gRPC/tRPC/Hono RPC/monorepos (~35%), multi-repo private consumers or external SDKs (~25-30%), running FastAPI/Express/Hono/Next.js/Go/Rails without already eliminating drift for $0 via FastAPI app.openapi() + git diff, Go Huma/Swaggo, @hono/zod-openapi, next-openapi-gen (https://github.com/tazo90/next-openapi-gen), or Rails committee (https://github.com/interagent/committee) (~35-40%), and willing to pay for a standalone CI binary collapses the qualified behavioral market to the ~1,000 Fermi bucket.

self_aware.justification: Unchanged at 0.5: API-first engineering teams shipping SDKs and multi-service REST APIs recognize OpenAPI drift and breaking changes as real operational risks, evidenced by active adoption of oasdiff, apidrifter, Schemathesis, SpecShield, and PactFlow, though not universal (1.0).

lucrative.justification: Unchanged at $1,000/yr: live pricing pages verify an allocated ~$900-$1,200/yr SMB dev-tool budget tier across SpecShield Team ($89/mo or $75/mo annual, https://specshield.io/pricing), PactFlow Team ($99/mo, https://pactflow.io/pricing), and oasdiff Pro ($100/mo, https://oasdiff.com/pricing), though BlastSpec cannot capture this budget at $79/mo against superior incumbents.

liquid.justification: Unchanged at 0.1 (upgraded believability from 0.4 to 0.7 on verified timelines and migration outcomes). By Nov 2026, Optic's Jan 12, 2026 archival (https://github.com/opticdev/optic), Postman's March 2026 Free cap (https://www.postman.com), and Anthropic's May 18, 2026 Stainless acquisition (https://www.stainless.com) are 6-10 months stale (DP15), and displaced Stainless users needed SDK code generation (migrating to Speakeasy https://www.speakeasy.com, Postman-acquired Fern https://buildwithfern.com, or Kiota), not a standalone CI linter. Buying remains episodic post-outage or annual tooling refresh.

eager_identity.justification: Reverted from 0.5 back to 0.1 (conceded by Advocate). GitHub Actions' default GITHUB_TOKEN is strictly single-repo scoped (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication). Cross-repo call-site scanning inside a local CI runner still requires injecting an org-wide PAT or GitHub App private key alongside an unvetted solo founder's binary — recreating the exact CI secret-exfiltration vector exploited in CVE-2025-30066 (tj-actions/changed-files, >23,000 repos exposed, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-30066). SOC 2-bound 10-30 eng teams will not audit thousands of lines of source-available multi-language AST code on every release SHA bump or trust an unvetted solo maintainer with org-wide secrets and merge-blocking CI gates.

eager_comparative.justification: Pinned at 0.1 (confirmed & worsened by primary verification). $0 oasdiff (https://oasdiff.com/pricing, https://github.com/oasdiff/oasdiff-action) already catches SDK-breaking operationId removals/modifications inline in PRs; $0 apidrifter (https://apidrifter.com) detects live code-to-OpenAPI drift across FastAPI, Express, and Hono with an MCP server; $0 Schemathesis (https://github.com/schemathesis/schemathesis) fuzz-tests live routes; SpecShield Team ($89/mo or $75/mo annual, https://specshield.io/pricing) undercuts BlastSpec's $79/mo annual price while shipping consumer registries, BDCT, and can-i-deploy gates; CodeRifts (https://coderifts.com) ships multi-protocol contract authorization with a $0 tier; Bump.sh ($50-$120/mo flat, https://bump.sh), PactFlow Team ($99/mo, https://pactflow.io/pricing), and oasdiff Pro ($100/mo) crowd the ceiling; and CodeRabbit Multi-Repo Analysis (https://www.coderabbit.ai) + Greptile (https://www.greptile.com, 500 free monthly credits for startups <=20 employees) bundle cross-repo breaking-change checks into general PR review.

enduring.justification: Unchanged at 0.5: preventing breaking API changes on every PR is a recurring operational need supporting subscription billing for incumbents (SpecShield, PactFlow, oasdiff Pro, Bump.sh), while near-zero switching cost (deleting one 8-line GitHub Actions workflow step) prevents 1.0 durability.

killed.reason: BAD_IDEA — KILL BLASTSPEC OUTRIGHT (BOTH SCENARIO A AND SCENARIO B). Rude Q&A exposed four fatal, irreconcilable defects and forced concessions on both softest Problem Score criteria (Plausible 10,000 -> 1,000; Eager-Identity 0.5 -> 0.1), collapsing the deterministic Problem Score from 0.02 to 0.0004 (1,000 × 0.5 × 1,000 × 0.1 × 0.1 × 0.1 × 0.5 ÷ 625,000) — 2,500x below the 1.0 viability bar: (1) Scenario B's 'zero-egress local CI binary' is mechanically self-defeating because GitHub Actions' single-repo GITHUB_TOKEN forces injecting an org-wide PAT or GitHub App private key into a runner executing an unvetted solo founder's binary (recreating CVE-2025-30066 supply-chain risk) while remaining physically unable to inspect external partner repos; (2) primary verification falsifies core differentiation ($0 oasdiff already detects api-operation-id-removed, $0 apidrifter checks live code-to-OpenAPI drift across FastAPI/Express/Hono with an MCP server, SpecShield Team at $75/mo annual undercuts BlastSpec's $79/mo with strictly more features, and CodeRabbit/Greptile bundle multi-repo breaking-change checks into general PR review with 500 free monthly startup credits); (3) native $0 spec sync in FastAPI, Go, Hono, and Next.js collapses the addressable market into the 1,000 bucket while 4-language static AST maintenance creates an immediate false-positive churn trap for a solo founder; and (4) the Jan-May 2026 Optic/Postman/Stainless catalyst is 6-10 months stale and mismatched to a non-SDK CI linter. Abandon completely; do not build or spend validation cycles attempting to rescue it.
